title: Microfluidic Channels Wax Priming
author: Jorge Fernández
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8hmht46

steps.title: Prepare Molten Wax
steps.instruction: Melt a small amount of wax from a wax pencil on a hot plate.

substeps.instruction: Set the hot plate to 105ºC or a temperature sufficient to melt the wax.
Cut a small amount of wax from a wax pencil and place it on a Petri dish.
Place the Petri dish on the hot plate and wait for the wax to melt.

steps.title: Prepare Nitrocellulose Membrane
steps.instruction: Cut nitrocellulose pieces to the appropriate size for the designed microfluidic path.

steps.title: Apply Wax to Stamp
steps.instruction: Coat the sealing ends of the plastic stamp with molten wax.

substeps.instruction: Immerse the sealing ends of the plastic stamp in the molten wax for 1-2 seconds.
Lift the stamp and verify that the stamping surface is fully covered in wax.

steps.title: Stamp Wax onto Membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer the wax from the stamp to the nitrocellulose membrane.

substeps.instruction: Quickly place the stamp against the membrane to release the wax onto the surface.
Apply mild pressure for 2-5 seconds, then lift the stamp.
If the membrane adheres to the stamp, softly touch the outer region of the sealed membrane to detach it.

steps.title: Heat-Treat to Prime Channels
steps.instruction: Heat the membrane to allow the wax to penetrate through the strip.

substeps.instruction: Cover the nitrocellulose strip with plastified paper (one sheet on top, one underneath).
Place the sandwich on the hot plate with a Petri dish (or any temperature-resistant flat object) on top to apply soft pressure.
Allow the strip to warm for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Cool and Inspect Membrane
steps.instruction: Cool the strip and verify the quality of the primed wax channels.

substeps.instruction: Remove the strip from the hot plate and let it cool.
Inspect for the shape of the channel and the presence of a thin 'white shadow' near the border of the wax imprimation.
Repeat the procedure if the channel is not wide enough or not uniform.
